policy.a_do_not_retry_unchanged_lesson_blocks: a mutation whose blocked_traits are all reproduced by the child genome, unless the child is tagged RETRY_WITH_CHANGED_CONDITION and names the changed condition
policy.retain_as_baseline_lessons_pin: the named seed candidates stay in the population for the whole search

lessons.title: The headline HML advantage was a prompt-envelope artifact
lessons.requirement: non-state prompt bytes must be byte-identical across arms

lessons.title: Prior HML syntax is not privileged among reasonable surfaces
Most measured accuracy was lexical
Serializer asymmetry can dominate the representation effect
Goal-centred ordering worsens locality
lessons.mechanism: relevance and dependency proximity are different relations
lessons.changed_condition_permitting_one_retry: the V2 runtime corpus carries real local contexts and reference edges; the prior corpus averaged 1.00 claims and zero dependencies

lessons.title: Dependency-topological ordering is a free improvement
Flat S-expressions destroy record-order error detection
lessons.requirement: error detection is reported per mutation family and never averaged before selection

lessons.title: Compression is a diagnostic, never the objective
lessons.requirement: token count is a Pareto axis, never a scalar objective

lessons.title: The line-based locality metric was an artifact
lessons.requirement: distances are measured in characters and tokens; lines are never a distance unit

lessons.title: The minimal-pair instrument saturated
lessons.requirement: an instrument whose arms all exceed 0.95 is reported as non-discriminative

lessons.title: The shipped renderer was non-deterministic
An opaque wrapper is not a semantic state
Derived structured projections were lossy where it mattered
lessons.requirement: the search reads elaborated Lean runtime identities, never a re-parse of pretty text

lessons.title: Real corpora can be too structurally trivial to discriminate
lessons.requirement: structural-richness statistics accompany every locality result

lessons.title: Trace provenance is not fresh replay
Generic structured representations sometimes matched or beat HML
lessons.note: stated in the mission brief; the only local measurement supporting it is FM-002's Stage-1 table. Not cited as an independent result.

lessons.title: Excessive compression is not automatically beneficial
lessons.note: held as a design principle and enforced by the Pareto vector; no local experiment measured a compression-induced accuracy loss.

lessons.title: Glyph token cost is a property of the vocabulary, not of the representation
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, pinned GPT-2 byte-level BPE
lessons.note: FM-004's escaping penalty reproduces under a second, independent vocabulary, so the UTF-8 hard gate is not an artifact of one tokenizer. The absolute token counts do not reproduce: every glyph the corpus needs is one token under Qwen3-8B and two or three under GPT-2. Any absolute token ranking is a statement about a vocabulary.
lessons.requirement: report token counts alongside bytes and tokenizer-free pre-tokens, and name the vocabulary in every token claim

lessons.title: Identifier-corruption detection saturates across every candidate
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, generation-zero seeds, 24 real V2 transitions
lessons.note: An altered identifier either fails to resolve or resolves to a different declaration, so every representation over an identity-carrying canonical state detects it. The axis was removed from Pareto selection before the search began and detect_drop_field took its place. detect_truncate_tail reads 0.000 for fifteen of sixteen seeds because the trailing block is usually the structured delta, which is outside the declared semantic contract; the one exception drops the delta entirely, which makes its tail contract content.
lessons.requirement: an instrument whose arms all saturate is reported as non-discriminative and excluded from selection, never reported as agreement

lessons.title: Goal linearization is unmeasurable on a corpus of single-goal states
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, pilot run, 317-transition V2 corpus
lessons.note: This is FM-014's problem in a new place and now quantified per axis. The V2 corpus is structurally rich in local context (mean 13.4 declarations, 63.4 intra-context references) so context_order moves the measurement 90% of the time, but it averages 1.01 goals per state, so every goal-linearization strategy renders identically. A ranking over graph_serialization from this corpus would be selection on noise.
lessons.requirement: report the share of single-axis mutations that changed the measurement, per axis, beside any claim about that axis; an axis at 0% is reported as unmeasurable on this corpus rather than as tied

lessons.title: Goal-centred ordering loses again, now on a corpus that has real dependencies
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, pilot run, 317-transition V2 corpus
lessons.note: FM-005 allowed exactly one retry on the stated changed condition that the V2 corpus carries real local-context dependency structure, unlike the prior corpus with 1.00 claims and zero dependencies. The retry was taken and the result reproduced: grouping declarations by relevance to the goal made binder-use distance worse, not better. The mechanism FM-005 named -- relevance and dependency proximity are different relations -- now has support from a corpus averaging 13.4 local declarations and 63.4 intra-context references.

lessons.title: Hoisting shared subterms into a DAG more than doubles token cost
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, pilot run, 317-transition V2 corpus
lessons.note: The intuition is that a subterm repeated n times should be written once. Measured, the alias table plus the reference machinery costs far more than the sharing saves on real Lean expression trees: elaborated subterms that repeat are mostly small, and the ones large enough to be worth hoisting are rarely repeated. It also halved record-order corruption detection, because an alias section separates a record from the content that identifies it.
lessons.changed_condition_permitting_one_retry: a corpus whose expression trees repeat large maximal subterms -- measure the repeat-size distribution before retrying

lessons.title: Naive substring matching inflated the locality metric
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, found while the definitive run was in progress
lessons.note: Short identity tokens are prefixes of longer ones. Searching for 'bf1' with a plain substring scan also matched inside 'bf10'..'bf19', overcounting mentions by 25% on the first transition checked and distorting every distance derived from them. Premise names had the same defect: 'Nat.add' matches inside 'Nat.add_comm'. Fixed by requiring a non-word character on both sides. The pilot run's locality figures were computed before this fix and are inflated; the definitive run is not comparable to them and the pilot's numbers are retained only as archived history.
lessons.requirement: identity and premise occurrences are counted with token boundaries, never with a plain substring scan

lessons.title: Cost and locality rank stably; corruption detection does not
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 representation search, finalists measured on SEARCH_DEV and on the never-selected SEARCH_VALIDATION split, and separately across 16+ Mathlib domains
lessons.note: Two independent checks agree. Across a held-out split selection never read, the cost and locality axes rank the finalists almost identically (rho 0.93-1.00) while record-swap detection nearly loses its ordering (rho 0.357). Across Mathlib domains, the same three axes have one leader in 100% of domains while the detection axes have a modal leader in only 56-69%. Cost and locality are properties of the representation; corruption detection depends on what the state happens to contain.
lessons.requirement: a corruption-detection claim names its sample and is reported with its cross-split rank correlation; a cost or locality claim may be stated for the representation

lessons.title: A colon heuristic made four of nine microtest suites read 100% unanswerable
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search V2, while building the structural-access suites
lessons.note: The suites decided whether to route an identity through the candidate's identity codec by testing whether the identity contained a colon. That was a guess about the shape of canonical identities, and it was wrong: the committed corpus uses short identities such as m9 and f17, so the test was false and the suite searched a rendering containing 'bm9' for the string 'm9'. Every identity now routes through the codec unconditionally, which returns unknown names unchanged and is therefore correct for both canonical identities and global constants like Nat.add. A second defect in the same family: the delta suite counted a goal identity found anywhere in the rendering as answering 'which goals did this step solve?', so a representation that omits the delta scored as if it stated it; relational queries are now scoped to the section that states the relation.
lessons.requirement: an instrument is checked against a real rendering before any number it produces is reported; a rate over zero queries is reported as zero queries, never as agreement

lessons.title: An invented axis can be accepted, registered, and completely inert
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search V2, first live generation
lessons.note: In the first live generation the model-driven meta-designer proposed three new axes with plausible mechanisms -- goal_refinement, context_signature, context_range -- and all three were accepted, registered, and bumped the genome schema to v2.3.0. All nine of their axis-value combinations then rendered IDENTICALLY. Two causes, both mine. First, the projection hooks matched value names literally ('GOAL_LOCAL', 'BEFORE'), so an axis whose inventor chose WIDE/NARROW took a fallback branch that happened to reproduce the existing layout; hooks now index behaviour by the value's position among the non-NONE values, so any naming works. Second, acceptance condition 6 -- 'at least one value differs observably on the corpus' -- was written in the spec and never enforced; registration now renders every value on a sample and rejects the axis as NO_OBSERVABLE_EFFECT if they all agree.
lessons.requirement: an invented axis is provisionally registered, then rendered at every value on a sample, and kept only if at least two values differ; an inert axis is worse than no axis because it consumes search budget and inflates the apparent size of the space

lessons.title: The validation gate mislabelled consistently-worse candidates as non-generalizing
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search V2, generation 1, seen in the live verdict stream
lessons.note: A child whose target metric got 2.2% worse on dev and 2.1% worse on validation was labelled NON_GENERALIZING_MUTATION and blocked from the elite population. Dev and validation agreed almost exactly; there was no dev-set claim for validation to fail to reproduce. The gate's job is specifically to catch improvements that exist only on dev, so a candidate that failed on both is a failed hypothesis and belongs to Pareto selection, which may still keep it for being best on a different axis. Blocking it let the validation gate silently override the selector.
lessons.requirement: the validation gate blocks eliteness only when a positive dev gain fails to reproduce; a hypothesis that failed on both splits is recorded as HYPOTHESIS_FAILED_CONSISTENTLY and left to the Pareto selector

lessons.title: Targeted acquisition closed the goal-ordering measurability gap FM-020 recorded
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search V2, after acquiring 1,125 structurally targeted transitions
lessons.note: FM-020 recorded that graph_serialization was mutated 11 times and changed the measurement zero times, because the corpus averaged 1.01 goals per state. The correct response was CORPUS_ACQUISITION, not another mutation. Scanning 250,814 LeanDojo transitions and selecting 1,125 for the strata the gap named raised the multi-goal share from 1.2% to 18.1% and the maximum from 2 goals to 12. On multi-goal states graph_serialization now separates into three distinct rendering groups -- BFS alone, GOAL_CENTRED alone, and the remaining five together -- and REORDER_GOAL_FOCUS, SWAP_GOAL_IDENTITY and CHANGE_SCOPE_PARENT went from 3% applicable to 100%. The axis was never uninformative; the corpus was unable to ask the question.
lessons.requirement: when an axis does not move the measurement, distinguish 'the axis does nothing' from 'this corpus cannot ask the question' before recording either, and prefer acquisition over further mutation when it is the second

lessons.title: The semantic corruption metric replaced bias with saturation
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search V2, 201 evaluated candidates over 14 generations
lessons.note: V1's corruption suite mutated rendered text, which measured syntax family as much as representation; V2 replaced it with mutation of the canonical state upstream of every candidate, which is the right architecture. But the detection PREDICATE was 'does the rendering change when the state is corrupted', and every representation of a changed state renders differently, so the metric read exactly 1.000 for all 201 evaluated candidates and contributed nothing to selection. Fixing the bias produced a saturated instrument, which is the FM-010 and FM-019 pattern for a third time. The predicate needs to be recoverability-based instead: does the candidate's own reader, given only the rendering, detect that a canonical well-formedness invariant is violated -- a context id that resolves to nothing, a focus order naming a goal that is not stated, an action citing a premise that is absent. binder_query_unanswerable and dependency_query_unanswerable are saturated at 0.000 for the same kind of reason and should be reported, not selected on.
lessons.requirement: before an instrument enters the selection axes, its spread across the current population is checked; an axis with one distinct value is reported as non-discriminative and excluded, exactly as FM-019 required for detect_corrupt_identity

lessons.title: The loop invented thirteen axes and none of them reached the frontier
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search V2, 14 generations on the 608-transition corpus
lessons.note: The open-ended machinery works: a model-driven meta-designer proposed axes the genome did not have, thirteen bound to executable projection hooks and passed the observable-effect gate, and the space grew from 4.095e19 to 1.548e26 points. But only five were exercised by a candidate that survived to evaluation, sixteen candidates carried one, and none of the six finalists uses one. The honest reading is that the capability is demonstrated and the payoff is not: on these selection axes, on this corpus, recombining existing axes still beat every invented one. Three plausible causes, untested: the invented axes were all layout transformations bound to two of four hooks and so explore a narrow region; new candidates get one generation to prove themselves against elites that have had many; and the corpus averaged 1.01 goals per state during this run, which is the condition FM-020 and FM-028 identify as hiding structural effects.
lessons.requirement: report invented axes by how many reached the frontier, not by how many were accepted; an accepted axis that no surviving candidate uses is machinery working and science not yet paying

lessons.title: Prefix sampling hid the corpus structure the acquisition campaign had just bought
lessons.measured_by: HML V3, preparing the generation-0 restart on the 918-transition search pool
lessons.note: FM-028 recorded that targeted acquisition closed FM-020's measurability gap: the new pool reaches twelve goals per state and is 19.0% multi-goal, against 1.01 mean goals and 1.2% before. The controller then sampled dev, microtest and mutation sets as PREFIXES of a list sorted by transition id. No prefix up to 128 rows contains a state with more than four goals, and the twelve-row mutation sample used to apply semantic corruption was 8.3% multi-goal -- close to the old corpus it replaced. The search would have been handed a structurally impoverished view of a corpus specifically acquired to be structurally rich, and would have re-derived FM-020 on data that had already fixed it. Caught before the run, by profiling the sample rather than the population.
lessons.requirement: report the profile of the SAMPLE, never the population, whenever claiming an axis is measurable; sample by structural stratum with a floor of one per non-empty stratum

lessons.title: The wrong ollama endpoint made a second meta-designer look like a model with nothing to say
lessons.measured_by: HML V3, adding a second zero-cost local meta-designer alongside gemma3:4b
lessons.note: Two independent defects, each of which silently produced zero proposals rather than an error. First, OllamaTransport posted to /api/generate, which bypasses the model's chat template; qwen38-rvn responded with a single token and an empty string on every prompt, while gemma3:4b tolerated it -- so the defect was invisible for as long as there was only one backend. Second, on /api/chat the model spent its entire 4096-token budget inside a <think> block and stopped on length before emitting any JSON. Prefilling a closed empty think block fixed it: 7 valid proposals in 67s, including the NEW_PRIMITIVE, INSTRUMENT_FIX and CORPUS_ACQUISITION types the rule-based proposer cannot make.
lessons.requirement: a backend returning an empty completion must raise with the stop reason and token count, never return an empty string that the loop records as a model with no proposals

lessons.title: Nine of thirty invented axes were the same axis under nine different names
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search, first 15 generations on the 918-transition pool, two meta-designer backends
lessons.note: FM-026 rejected axes that change nothing. This is its sibling: an axis that DOES change the rendering, passes the observable-effect gate, and is a perfect copy of one already registered. action_scope, dependency_capsule, goal_id_projection, hash_projection, local_context_fragment, local_dependency_capsule, local_dependency_scope, semantic_context_grouping and semantic_summary were all neighbourhood_capsule with empty params over NONE/GOAL_LOCAL/ACTION_LOCAL. Measured directly: two such axes render identically to each other, and applying both is idempotent with applying one, so they are one dimension registered nine times. Three consequences, all bad. The reported search-space size is a product over axes, so each copy multiplied it by three while adding no reachable rendering -- the space figure was inflated by 6561x from this group alone. The Pareto front fills with candidates that differ by candidate_id and not by output. And structural convergence is unreachable by construction, because a meta-designer can always mint a fresh NAME for an axis that already exists; the run showed no sign of the invention rate declining across 15 generations. The system brief's own worked example is dependency_capsule, which is where the models were copying the shape from.
lessons.requirement: an invented axis must be rejected unless its set of renderings differs from every axis already in the genome; compare behaviour, not the (hook, params, values) signature, since different hooks or value names can still reach the same renderings

lessons.title: Blocking duplicate axes turned FM-030's negative around: an invented axis reached the finalists
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search, 106 generations to structural convergence on the 918-transition pool, three meta-designer backends
lessons.note: FM-030 recorded that thirteen invented axes were accepted and none reached the frontier, and offered three untested explanations. With the FM-033 duplicate gate in place the picture inverts. Of 289 axis proposals only 5 were genuinely new dimensions; 205 were behavioural duplicates that the old gate would have registered. Two of the seven finalists now carry an invented axis, both values of `dependency_capsule`: R_159628756bc5 (GOAL_LOCAL) is the cheapest candidate under all four tokenizer vocabularies, and R_fcd13f8d56a5 (ACTION_LOCAL) reaches 11.844 dependency-query token distance against roughly 27.8 for the others, a 57% reduction. The axis that paid is the one the meta-designers kept re-proposing under fresh names; registering it once and blocking the copies is what let it be evaluated on its merits instead of diluting the population with 205 aliases of itself. FM-030's negative is superseded for this configuration; its caution about reporting axes by how many reach the frontier stands.
lessons.requirement: report invented axes as (accepted, duplicate, unimplementable, reaching the frontier); the first number alone is meaningless

lessons.title: A mid-run churn rate is not evidence that a convergence criterion cannot be met
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 open-ended search, generations 50-106
lessons.note: At generation 70 the frontier position had been frozen for ten generations and the genome for fifty, but exact frontier membership was still churning at a mean of 2.3 entrants per generation with no visible downward trend. The reading taken from that was that the membership clause was unsatisfiable by construction -- eighteen children and three novelty slots per generation into a 1e19-point space must always yield fresh Pareto-equivalent points -- and a weaker clause based on the stability of the reported shortlist was drafted to replace it. That reading was wrong. Churn kept declining; generations 101 to 105 had no entrant and no departure at all, and the run converged on the original criterion at generation 106. The weaker clause was reverted unused. The general form of the error: a rate observed while a search is still improving does not extrapolate, and a criterion that is merely slow to satisfy is indistinguishable from one that cannot be satisfied until it is satisfied. The duplicate-name case (FM-033) IS genuinely unsatisfiable and the difference is that there the generator is unbounded and the blocking condition never approaches its target; here the quantity was monotonically approaching zero and only the last few steps were missing.
lessons.requirement: before weakening a stopping criterion, show that the blocking quantity is not trending toward the threshold; a flat extrapolation from a mid-run window is not that showing

lessons.title: The reproducibility verifier could not see invented axes, and reported the gap as non-determinism
lessons.measured_by: HML V3, verifying the converged 106-generation run
lessons.note: verify_reproducibility.py renders each candidate in a fresh subprocess under a different PYTHONHASHSEED and compares digests. It built every compiler from the genome alone, with no invented axes and no primitive registry, on BOTH sides -- so for the 92 candidates carrying an invented axis it verified a different object from the one the search evaluated. It also keyed the child's results by the genome's own candidate_id rather than by the record id; an invented-axis candidate shares its base genome with its parent, so the lookup silently returned None and was counted as a mismatch. The visible symptom was 'NOT REPRODUCIBLE: 2 candidates differ across processes', which is the most alarming possible way for a verifier to report its own blind spot. Both candidates were invented-axis carriers. After passing the invented values and the registry to the child and keying by record id, 60 candidates including 10 carriers verify with zero mismatches. Any earlier reproducibility claim covered only candidates without invented axes.
lessons.requirement: a verifier must construct the object under test the same way the search constructed it, including every layer the search added; and it must key results by the identifier the search uses, not by a derived one that can collide

lessons.title: Two microtest stresses were built on an ordering the semantic contract declares to be a set
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 MicroMath Lab V1 construction
lessons.note: PREMISE and ACTION_ARGUMENT were first built by permuting action.external_premise_refs and action.local_context_refs. projection.semantic_core stores both as sorted() -- the declared contract treats them as SETS and order carries no meaning. Every one of the eleven representations, all four controls included, therefore 'failed' those cells: ACTION_ARGUMENT rendered byte-identically for A and B, and PREMISE rendered differently but decoded to the same object. Read naively that was a spectacular finding, a universal representation weakness across the whole space. It was a benchmark bug. Both stresses were rebuilt on set MEMBERSHIP, which is semantic, and all eleven then scored 29/29 expressible.
lessons.requirement: a counterfactual must change projection.semantic_core; assert it, because a transposition the contract calls a no-op produces a question with no ground truth and reports it as a representation failure

lessons.title: An aggregate shortcut audit hid two cells that a dumb rule solved perfectly
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 MicroMath Lab V1, per-stress shortcut audit
lessons.note: The audit reported 0.62 against a 0.65 limit and read as a pass. Split by stress it was not: MULTI_GOAL and PREMISE both scored 1.000 for 'pick whichever option appears earlier'. MULTI_GOAL leaked because the counterfactual swapped the goals' positions as well as the focus, so the focused goal was always written first; PREMISE leaked because the replacement premise was drawn from source metadata no renderer emits, so presence alone answered the question. Six of eight cells were sound and their soundness diluted the two that were not. MICROMATH section 8 says the cell is the primitive diagnostic unit; that applies to the audit as much as to the results.
lessons.requirement: audit shortcuts per cell, never only in aggregate; a benchmark is only as valid as its weakest cell

lessons.title: The audit and the probe disagreed about how an identity is spelled, and the audit read clean because of it
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 MicroMath Lab V1
lessons.note: Identities reach the page through the candidate's identity codec: canonical m3 is written bm3, and declarations can appear under display names. The shortcut audit counted occurrences of the RAW canonical ids. Those are absent from the rendering, so both counts were zero, every item scored as undecided, and the audit returned a spotless 0.509 for a benchmark it had not examined at all. The same mismatch would have handed the model a choice between two strings not present in the text it was shown. Both the audit and the probe now encode options through the same codec.
lessons.requirement: whatever an instrument counts must be the same string the subject is shown; a clean score from an instrument that matched nothing is indistinguishable from a clean score from an instrument that worked

lessons.title: Ranking base states by richness made the benchmark unprobeable and collapsed its diversity
lessons.measured_by: HML V3 MicroMath Lab V1 construction
lessons.note: Selecting the structurally richest eligible state per cell chose the largest states: median LEAN_LIKE rendering 16,158 pre-tokens, only 11 of 29 fitting a 16k context. A diagnostic no reader can be run on cannot answer the question the lab exists to ask. Adding a size budget fixed that but then concentrated 45 cells onto 17 base states, nine of which spanned two splits, so MICRO_HIDDEN shared its mathematics with MICRO_DEV and could not have measured generalisation. Preferring unused base states restored 45 distinct states for 45 cells, and splits are now assigned by base state so a state cannot straddle one.
lessons.requirement: a microbenchmark has three constraints at once -- the cell must be answerable, the item must fit the reader, and the splits must not share mathematics; optimising any one alone breaks another
